newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher after, subdued activity.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher after, subdued activity.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Tuesday after a bounce in the market from its slump on Monday.
"Justifiably, the market adjusted," said a trader at a foreign bank. The bounce came as the U.S. Treasury market remained stable through Tuesday's session.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/4 to 89-5/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 126.00.
Traders said the market is set to turn its attention back to the U.S. market on Wednesday with the release of U.S. consumer prices.
"The market will follow what happens in the U.S.," said another trader.
The consumer price release will be another important figure for the Federal Reserve in its consideration on monetary policy on March 25.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.93 percent from 5.98 percent.
